topic.name: Calculating Acceleration for Straight-Line Motion Using Differentiation

question.text: The displacement $s$ of a particle moving in a straight line is given by $s(t)=12t^4 - 3t^3 +t.$ Find the particle's acceleration at time $t.$
question.explanation:
First, we calculate $v(t)$ by differentiating $s(t)\mathbin{:}$ \[ \begin{align} v(t) &= \dfrac{\textrm{d}s}{\textrm{d}t}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}(12t^4 - 3t^3 +t)\\[5pt] &= 48t^3-9t^2+1 \end{align} \]

Now, we differentiate $v(t)$ to find $a(t)\mathbin{:}$ \[ \begin{align} a(t) &=\dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}t}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}(48t^3-9t^2+1)\\[5pt] &= 144t^2-18t \end{align} \]

question.text: The displacement $s$ of a particle moving in a straight line is given by $s(t) = \dfrac {7}{t^3} + t^2.$ Find the particle's acceleration at time $t.$
question.explanation:
First, we calculate $v(t)$ by differentiating $s(t)\mathbin{:}$

\[ \begin{align} v(t) &= \dfrac{\textrm{d}s}{\textrm{d}t}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left(\dfrac {7}{t^3} + t^2\right)\\[5pt] &= -\dfrac {21}{t^4} + 2t \end{align} \]

Now, we differentiate $v(t)$ to find $a(t)\mathbin{:}$ \[ \begin{align} a(t) &=\dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}t}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left(-\dfrac {21}{t^4} + 2t\right)\\[5pt] &= \dfrac {84}{t^5} + 2 \end{align} \]

example.title: Calculating the Acceleration of a Particle Given Its Velocity

question.text: The velocity $v$ (in $\textrm{m/s}$) of a particle at time $t$ (in seconds) is given by $v(t) = \left( t \ln t + 4t \right).$ Calculate the velocity of the particle when the acceleration $a$ is equal to $6 \,\textrm{m/s}^2.$
question.explanation:
We differentiate $v(t)$ to calculate $a(t)\mathbin{:}$ \[ \begin{align} a(t) &=\dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}t}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t} \left( t \ln t + 4t \right) \\[5pt] &= \ln t +1 +4\\[5pt] &=5+\ln t \end{align} \]

To calculate the time when the acceleration is $a=6,$ we substitute this into the above:

\[ \begin{align} 6 &= 5+\ln t\\[3pt] \ln t&=1\\[3pt] e^{\left(\ln t\right)}&=e^{1}\\[3pt] t&=e \end{align} \]

Then, to calculate the velocity at time $t=e,$ we substitute this into the equation for the velocity: \[ \begin{align} v(e) &=\left( e \ln e + 4e \right)\\[3pt] &=e(1)+4e\\[3pt] &=5e \textrm{ m/s} \end{align} \]

Therefore, the velocity when $a=6 \,\textrm{m/s}^2$ is $5e \textrm{ m/s}.$

example.title: Calculating the Acceleration of a Particle Given Its Velocity

question.text: The velocity $v$ of a particle at time $t$ is given by $v(t) = 3t^{3}+6t^{2}-5t.$ Calculate the acceleration $a$ of the particle at time $t.$
question.explanation: We differentiate $v(t)$ to calculate $a(t) \mathbin{:}$ \[ \begin{align} a(t) &=\frac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}t}\\[5pt] &= \frac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left(3t^{3}+6t^{2}-5t \right)\\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{9t^{2}+12t-5} \end{align} \]
